framing_options: OPTION A - KEEP (baseline, sharpen price): Flat-top ('truncated'/crown) attic trusses at 600mm centres, hip ends as multi-ply hip girder + mono attic/jack set. This is how every UK fabricator actually frames a hipped crown roof with habitable space - the flat 28m2 deck IS the truncated top chord, no separate flat structure needed. For 8.6 x 6.0m at 41 deg: ~9-11 flat-top attic trusses (2026 market GBP 130-260 each for spans in this class - MyJobQuote/Checkatrade put attic trusses at GBP 80-170 supply, ~GBP 163 avg for an 8m-span attic truss) + hip girders (multi-ply, GBP 600-900) + monos/jacks/loose timber. Realistic supplied range GBP 5,500-7,500. The current GBP 7,500 supply line is at the TOP of the plausible band - a 3-4 quote tender should land GBP 6,000-6,800, saving GBP 700-1,500. Erection GBP 3,500-4,500 stands (hand-set from hiab is normal for this weight class).

OPTION B - KILL: Standard attic trusses + site-cut flat deck over. No supply saving - fabricators price the flat top chord into the truss for pennies (it is LESS timber than a full apex), and a site-built deck adds 2-3 carpenter days (GBP 600-900) plus a structural interface Building Control will want calcs for. Strictly worse than A.

OPTION C - PRICE AS ALTERNATE: Girder + hip sets + fully LOOSE infill hips (girder truss supports site-cut loose timber infill - standard fabricator detail for spans up to ~5.7m per the Trussform/Minera technical guides, and these hip ends are well inside that). Supplied package drops to ~GBP 5,000-6,300 because you delete the factory monos/jacks; adds ~GBP 500-800 site carpentry cutting jacks. Net saving GBP 300-600 ONLY if the carpenter's price-work rate absorbs the cutting - ask both fabricator and carpenter to price it. Worth carrying as tender alternate, not a banker.

OPTION D - KILL: Posi-rafter / roof cassettes. Panelised and posi systems carry a 20-40% one-off premium (they pay back on volume sites and crane-set programmes; you have no crane and one roof). Expect GBP 9k-12k supplied. Dead on arrival for a cheapness-first client.

OPTION E - KILL: Full site-cut roof on steels. Steel ridge/purlin schemes for habitable roofs run GBP 8k-18k for the steel-and-rebuild work alone (structuralengineercalcs/bestbuilders 2026 guides) before you cut a single rafter; carpentry-heavy at GBP 6k+ and slower. Attic trusses exist precisely to beat this.

HIP PREMIUM (info only, geometry fixed): the two hip ends vs a gabled equivalent add ~GBP 1,200-1,800 supplied (multi-ply girders, mono/jack sets, extra metalwork) plus 1-2 days erection - a 15-25% premium on the package, consistent with fabricator guidance that hips are the most expensive truss configuration.

SPACING ECONOMICS: 600mm centres is the cost floor - moving to 400 adds ~45% more truss units for only marginally lighter chords and nearly always nets out dearer on a one-off. BUT attic FLOOR deflection on long clear spans is what forces fabricators to 400 or to fatter bottom chords; if the floor chord can pick up a mid-span masonry cross-wall bearing (see structural_ve) the design stays at 600 with minimum chord sizes. Instruct 600 centres as the default and make any fabricator proposing 400 show it cheaper in pounds.

TR26 MARKET 2026: soft. Forest Research softwood sawlog index was down 4.4% in real terms to Sep 2025 (GBP 59.70/m3) and merchant TR26 prices (e.g. Beesley & Fildes 47x200 at ~GBP 13/length ex VAT) show no inflation pressure. There is no timber-market excuse for a fabricator padding the quote - tender hard now; no benefit to waiting.
structure.tender_strategy: Get 4 quotes minimum; one-off attic packages routinely spread 20-40% between plants on identical designs because pricing tracks factory loading, not cost. Target list: Donaldson Timber Engineering (multiple Midlands plants; Donaldson Direct advertises 5-working-day delivery on standard product, attic crown package realistically 2-3 weeks), Pasquill (nearest branch to B14; published lead time 10 working days manufacture, 5-day delivery turnaround), Midland Timber Engineering (Walsall - closest, cheapest delivery), Harlow Timber Systems (Long Eaton), plus one online independent such as Tailor Made Designs (instant online quoting, 5-10 day attic lead) purely as a price fence. WHAT GETS THE SHARPEST PRICE: send the approved planning drawings PLUS a one-page truss enquiry sheet - dimensioned roof plan and section, 41.0 deg pitch, crown/flat outline with the 28m2 deck level, ridge cap at 7.52m, tile dead load stated as concrete interlocking ~50-55 kg/m2, habitable floor loading 1.5 kN/m2 + partitions, ALL bearing positions including internal masonry cross-walls (this is the single biggest price lever - without it they design worst-case clear span), wall plate levels, 600mm centres as default, hiab off-load / no crane note, and required delivery week. Ask every fabricator for TWO prices: (i) all-truss hip ends, (ii) hip girder + loose infill with jacks cut on site - and state supply-only, design free, delivery included. Do not pay a design deposit; every mainstream fabricator designs free to win the order. LEAD TIME AUG 2026: design + connector approval 1-2 weeks, manufacture 5-10 working days - order by early/mid September for a guaranteed October set; capacity is slack (housebuilding still subdued), which is exactly when one-off spreads widen and hungry plants undercut, so the fourth quote is where the saving usually appears.
structure.tile_verdict: The GBP 4,150 line (~GBP 14-15/m2 supplied Edgemere-class + price-work laying) is close to the floor but not quite on it. Facts verified: Marley Edgemere/Duo Edgemere are 9.7-10.6 tiles/m2 single-lap flat 'plain-effect' interlockers with 17.5 deg minimum pitch - 41 deg is comfortably compliant with headroom to spare. Cheaper compliant swaps that keep the appearance: (1) Russell Grampian or Breedon/Forticrete equivalent flat through-colour interlocker at 9.8-10.6 tiles/m2 - typically GBP 1.00-1.30/tile via SIG/independents, i.e. GBP 10-13.5/m2, saving GBP 150-300 on 75m2 - take it only if a merchant quote beats Edgemere like-for-like, since the visual difference at 41 deg from the street is nil; (2) seconds/overstock pallets (Roofing Outlet, HG Roofing and similar sell Edgemere-family pallets of 240; clearance batches run GBP 0.80-1.10/tile = GBP 8-11/m2) - viable ONLY if all ~800 tiles + fittings come from one colour batch; on 75m2 of street-facing 41 deg roof a batch mismatch destroys the kerb-appeal covenant, so buy 4 pallets same-batch or walk; (3) reclaimed single-lot - Birmingham Gumtree shows concrete interlockers at GBP 0.40-0.50/tile (GBP 4-5/m2) but an 800-tile single-profile single-colour lot is rare, carries no warranty and reads as 'used' up close: KILL for this client. FIXINGS (BS 5534, real cost item): at 41 deg (below the 55 deg all-clip threshold) in the Birmingham wind zone, single-lap interlockers need every tile mechanically fixed (nail) with clips to perimeter/eaves/verge courses and any calc-driven field clipping; clip cost between the Edgemere class and a standard flat interlocker is essentially identical (same format, same clips), so the tile family choice does NOT move the fixing bill - but confirm the price-work rate INCLUDES nails/clips and a manufacturer fixing spec, because a bolted-on clipping extra is a GBP 250-400 surprise. NET: keep Edgemere-class as specified, run one merchant check on Grampian-class and same-batch overstock; realistic best-case saving GBP 200-400, not a re-spec event.
structure.flat_verdict: The GBP 1,500 EPDM line IS effectively the floor - keep it and protect it. Numbers: 28m2 at GBP 1,500 = GBP 54/m2 all-in, versus 2026 market installed EPDM at GBP 80-120/m2 (BookaBuilder/BestBuilders/Butler guides); a supply-only ClassicBond/Elevate(Firestone) kit for 28m2 (membrane, deck adhesive, trims, corners - a 6.1m-wide roll does it in ONE piece, zero field seams) runs ~GBP 450-650 from Rubber4Roofs/UK Flat Roofing/Roofing Outlet, leaving GBP 850-1,050 for a 1-1.5 day two-man lay - tight but real trade money. Alternatives all lose: torch-on 3-layer felt is the only nominally cheaper system (GBP 55-95/m2 installed, materials ~GBP 10-14/m2) but saves at most GBP 200-300 while importing hot-works on an occupied busy-road site, hot-works insurance conditions during the build, a 15-20 year life vs 40-50 for EPDM, and a covering surveyors already flag - KILL; GRP is dearer (GBP 95-140/m2 installed), weather-dependent and brittle over a 28m2 timber deck's movement - KILL; single-ply PVC runs GBP 85-135/m2 and needs an approved installer for any warranty - no saving at this area - KILL. Insurer/lender view: EPDM on a domestic warm deck is mainstream and mortgageable (Property118 lender commentary, Full View flat-roof inspection guidance) - insurers care about the flat-area percentage and condition, not the EPDM brand; the hidden 28m2 crown changes nothing since it was declared in the design. Only genuine VE inside the line: confirm the warm-deck PIR insulation for the flat centre is not double-counted between the EPDM line and the Part L insulation package, spec a single-piece 1.2mm membrane (no seams = no callbacks), and make the kit supplier price the kerb/upstand trims into the kit rather than the flashing line.
structure.structural_ve: Three levers, one big. (1) SPAN DIRECTION - THE BIG ONE, KEEP: the trusses should span the 6.0m depth, bearing on the two 8.6m-long walls (new rear wall and the original house rear wall with padstones/spreader plate as needed), NOT the 8.6m width between flanks. A 6.0m-span attic truss uses dramatically smaller chords than an 8.6m one (attic truss price scales hard with clear span - the GBP 163 market average is for 8m; a 6m attic truss sits nearer GBP 120-150). If the current GBP 7,500 supply figure was built on an 8.6m span, flipping the span direction alone plausibly takes GBP 1,000-2,000 out of the package. Verify the existing house wall can take the bearing (mature cavity masonry almost always can with padstones - engineer's letter, ~GBP 250 if not already covered) and instruct the fabricators to design 6.0m span. (2) MASONRY CROSS-WALL MID-BEARING - KEEP IF THE PLAN HAS ONE: any GF-FF masonry cross-wall carried up to underside of floor chords gives the attic floor a mid-span bearing, keeps the design at 600mm centres with minimum chords, and costs nothing (the wall is already in the bill). Declare every internal loadbearing wall on the truss enquiry - free money, worth 10-15% of the package. (3) STEEL RIDGE/PERIMETER BEAM INSTEAD OF GIRDER TRUSSES - KILL: a fitted steel in this roof runs GBP 1,500-2,500+ (supply, hiab handling into a crown, connection details, fire protection at three-storey) versus GBP 600-900 for the multi-ply girders already inside the truss package, and it adds a trade and a programme dependency. The truss package IS the cheap structure; do not break it open. Net structural VE target: GBP 1,000-2,500 off the supplied package, all lawful, all within standard TR26/BS 5268-EC5 fabricator design, nothing that touches the fixed external geometry.

details.insulation_buildup: CHEAPEST COMPLIANT BUILD-UPS TO U 0.15 (2026 prices). (A) PITCHED SKIRT / SLOPING CEILING (attic-truss top chords, 600cc): 120mm PIR (lambda 0.022) friction-fitted between chords + 37.5-50mm PIR insulated plasterboard under, joints foil-taped as the VCL = U ~0.14-0.15 incl. 10% timber bridging. Materials at BRANDED-SECONDS prices: 120mm seconds PIR ~GBP 11-13/m2 (vs GBP 13-15 firsts, e.g. 120mm Celotex GBP 36-43/board = GBP 12.50-15/m2) + insulated plasterboard GBP 12-17/m2 = ~GBP 24-30/m2 vs ~GBP 32-38 all-branded. SECONDS VERDICT: yes, seconds channels are fine HERE with one condition - buy identifiable branded seconds (Seconds & Co is the approved Kingspan/Celotex seconds outlet, Mid Wales, delivers nationwide; eBay pallet sellers also serve Birmingham) where the facer print shows brand/thickness/declared lambda 0.022. Building control accepts them in the U-calc because they are the same certified product with cosmetic defects; keep delivery notes + facer photos for the BC file. Do NOT use unbranded 'eco'/recovered boards of unknown lambda in compliance layers. Expect 1-4mm thickness variance - design the calc at nominal minus tolerance if the BCO is picky. (B) HYBRID (wool + PIR): 140-150mm mineral wool frame batt between chords (GBP 5-7/m2) + 62.5mm insulated plasterboard under gets ~0.16-0.17 - it MISSES 0.15 unless you go to 72.5mm laminate, and the thicker laminate erases the wool saving on the slopes. Wool only wins where depth is free: ashlar/knee stud walls (140mm batt + standard board, ~GBP 8-10/m2) and any residual cold-loft triangles (400mm loft roll GBP 3-4/m2). Use PIR on slopes, wool in the verticals. (C) 28m2 FLAT CENTRE - WARM DECK ONLY: 18mm OSB3 deck, sealed VCL (self-adhesive bitumen or fully lapped/taped polythene), 150mm flat-roof PIR (lambda 0.022 = U ~0.147) mechanically fixed/bonded, then EPDM (direct-bond to insulation facer or over 11mm OSB overlay per the EPDM kit spec). 150mm PIR firsts GBP 41-54/board = GBP 14-19/m2; seconds ~GBP 10-13/m2 (~GBP 300-400 for the 28m2 at seconds rates). COLD DECK RULING: not literally banned in England (it is in Scotland), but BS 6229:2018 and BS 5250 say avoid; AD L pushes all new coverings to warm deck; NHBC/warranty providers refuse it for new work - and on a CROWN roof it is physically a non-starter: the flat centre is landlocked by 41-degree slopes with no opposing eaves, so the mandatory 50mm cross-ventilated void cannot be achieved. Cold deck here = uninsurable and un-signable. The warm-deck premium over a notional cold deck is only ~GBP 300-450 of PIR anyway. VENTILATION/VCL for the pitched part: see sundries - crown roofs have no ridge to vent, so the strategy matters.
details.dryfix_verdict: MORTAR-ONLY IS DEAD: BS 5534:2014(+A2:2018) has required mechanical fixing of every ridge/hip unit EVEN IF mortar-bedded since 2014; the only exception is baby ridge/hip on details under 3m (porches/bays). BS 8612:2018 is the product standard dry-fix kits must meet - LABC and the Roof Tile Association confirm contractors must use BS 8612-compliant systems. So the real choice is (a) dry-fix kit vs (b) mortar bed PLUS clamps/screws into a ridge batten - mortar alone fails building control and NHBC. GEOMETRY NOTE: a crown roof has no conventional ridge - the tiles die into the flat-centre perimeter (an upstand/drip trim detail in the EPDM package, not a ridge line). The line item is HIPS ONLY: 4 hips at roughly 5-5.5m = ~20-22 lm. COSTS 2026: dry-fix materials - Klober economy 6m dry ridge kit GBP 56 ex VAT, Manthorpe 6m GBP 63 ex VAT; universal dry HIP kits with trays/clamps run ~GBP 10-14/lm in materials, so ~GBP 220-300 for this roof. Labour: Midlands price-work roofers charge ~GBP 12-18/lm to fit dry hip (fast, no wet trade); mortar+mechanical is ~GBP 8-10/lm labour plus mortar pennies but slower overall (mixing, bedding, then still clamping every unit) and carries the repointing/callback liability. Contractor supply-and-fit quotes of GBP 35-65/lm for dry ridge/hip are the retail number - on price-work with free-issue kit you pay materials + GBP 12-18/lm. VERDICT: dry-fix the hips. Total swing between the two lawful routes is under GBP 200 on 20 lm; dry-fix is maintenance-free, insurer-friendly, and faster on the scaffold. Budget ~GBP 500-600 all-in for hip fixing.
details.sundries: MEMBRANE: cheapest compliant = budget W1-class breather at 100-115gsm, BS 5534 wind-zone rated (Birmingham is a low wind zone, standard laps fine): Novia Black+ Ultra ~GBP 38-45 per 75m2 roll, generic/overstock 1m x 50m rolls GBP 25-35 on eBay/clearance = GBP 0.55-0.90/m2 - two rolls cover the skirt for under GBP 90. Cromar Vent3 (GBP 50-60/roll) only if the BCO wants a named BBA cert. CRITICAL for room-in-roof: a standard airtight-class membrane over an unventilated warm slope needs a 25mm+ vent gap above the PIR PLUS high/low ventilation, OR you use an air-open (LR) membrane per its BBA cert with no gap. Crown roof has NO RIDGE to vent, so the cheap lawful route is: over-fascia eaves vent (10-25mm airflow, GBP 3-5/lm) at the bottom + 6-8 in-line tile vents high on each slope near the crown (GBP 25-35 each) + 25mm gap above the between-rafter PIR; belt-and-braces is the taped foil-faced PIR laminate ceiling acting as a proper VCL per BS 5250 - that VCL is non-negotiable either way. BATTENS: must be BS 5534 GRADED and stamped (the stamp/colour is a brand mark - JB Red etc.; 'graded' is the legal requirement, blue/red irrelevant): 25x50 graded ~GBP 0.85-1.10/lm in 2026; 75m2 at 345mm gauge = ~220 lm + waste = GBP 200-260. FIXINGS: interlocking tiles do NOT need every-tile nailing - run the free Marley/Redland fixing-spec calculator; typically nail alternate courses + clip all perimeter/eaves/verge courses: GBP 150-250 in ring-shank nails and clips. EAVES: felt support/eaves protection tray GBP 2-3/lm, comb filler for the tile profile GBP 1/lm. TOTAL SUNDRIES BUDGET: ~GBP 700-950 for this roof - anything above GBP 1,000 in a quote is padding.
details.labour_rates: TILING: 2026 national guides say GBP 40-60/m2 'labour' but that is contractor supply-and-fix framing; genuine Midlands PRICE-WORK gangs lay big-format interlocking concrete at GBP 18-30/m2 labour-only (Edgemere-class thin-edge interlocking sits mid-range, ~GBP 22-28/m2, because of the neater bond), plus hip/valley cutting premium GBP 10-20/lm. This roof: 75m2 x ~GBP 25 = GBP 1,875 + 20-22 lm hips x GBP 15 = ~GBP 300 → GBP 2,100-2,400 labour. Tiles at GBP 14-15/m2 supplied = GBP 1,050-1,200; with sundries GBP 700-950 the existing GBP 4,150 tile line is honest with maybe GBP 300-500 of fat - hold it, but fix the m2 and lm rates IN WRITING. DAYWORK TRAP: roofer day rate GBP 200-275 + labourer GBP 120-150; a hipped 75m2 skirt on daywork drifts to 8-10 days = GBP 3,000-4,000 for the same tiling. Never convert to daywork mid-job 'because of the hips' - the hip premium is already priced per lm. ROOFLINE: contractor supply-and-fit runs GBP 90-150/lm, but unbundled: 18mm uPVC square fascia GBP 8-12/lm + vented soffit GBP 6-10/lm supply, carpenter fits at GBP 8-12/lm; ~20-21m of roofline (three sides, rear extension) = GBP 450-650 materials + GBP 400-600 labour. UBIFLEX vs LEAD: Code 4 lead is GBP 17-26/lm by width (450mm x 3m = GBP 79 inc VAT); Ubiflex B3 3.5mm 6m rolls run roughly GBP 45-75/roll by width = ~40-60% of lead like-for-like, no scrap-theft value (real risk on a low accessible rear extension), lighter, no specialist leadworker rate - a general roofer fits it. Abutment flashings on this footprint save GBP 150-250 vs lead. VERDICT ON THE GBP 1,800 LINE (Ubiflex + fascia + RWG): plausible but squeezable to ~GBP 1,400-1,500 by free-issuing materials and paying fit-only rates. Whole-roof labour reality check: nothing in the GBP 18,500 bill is scandalous; the recoverable margin across labour lines is ~GBP 800-1,200, taken by written price-work rates and free-issued materials, not by changing spec.
details.rainwater: Standard 112mm half-round uPVC is ALREADY the cheapest system that does not look cheap - supply GBP 2-3.50/lm (4m lengths GBP 8-14), fittings GBP 3-6 each, fitted rates GBP 5-10/lm labour on top of the fascia visit (guides quote GBP 30-60/lm supplied and fitted as a standalone trade - avoid that by bundling with the roofline carpenter). Do NOT drop to 68mm 'mini' gutter - undersized on a 75m2/41-degree catchment and reads as conservatory-grade from the pavement. Do NOT pay for cast-iron-effect or ogee here: this is a REAR extension - the street sees at most a sliver of fascia line past the house, so black or anthracite half-round holds the luxury read at bottom cost (black hides better than white against a tiled skirt and does not yellow). HIDDEN-SIDE SPEC DROP: keep one branded system (FloPlast/Brett Martin class) on any return visible from Vicarage Road for crisp mouldings and colour-fastness, and use the merchant's economy own-brand of the SAME 112mm half-round profile on the fully hidden rear runs - profiles are near-universal and adaptors exist, but stay one brand per continuous run so joints seal. Hydraulics: two 68mm downpipes (one per rear corner) comfortably drain the skirt; the 28m2 flat centre discharges via the EPDM outlet/chute onto the lower slope or an internal outlet - confirm the EPDM kit includes the outlet so it is not a variation later. Budget: ~GBP 180-280 materials + GBP 150-250 fitting for the whole RWG = well inside the existing line.
details.sequencing: SCAFFOLD COMPRESSION: critical path is trusses → membrane/batten → EPDM upstand → tile → flashings → roofline/RWG. (1) Attic trusses at 8.6m span are 150-250kg each - hand-setting off the hiab needs a 4-5 man lift crew and clear deck; a priced 2-day set + 2-3 days bracing keeps carpentry at the GBP 3,500 end - agree a fixed erect price, not day rate, and have the hiab land trusses on prepared bearers at wall-plate level in ONE delivery (busy road = one early-morning lane occupation, not three). (2) Tile loading: ~730 Edgemere-class tiles (~3.3t) - cheapest is the merchant's hiab to the scaffold first lift on delivery (usually free or GBP 50-80); a conveyor hire (GBP 100-150/day, half-day is enough) beats two labourers hand-passing (GBP 250-300/day) only if the hiab cannot reach - order tiles, battens, membrane and hip kits on the SAME hiab drop. (3) SINGLE ROOFING SUB FOR EPDM + TILING: yes - the crown perimeter detail (EPDM trim/upstand woven under the top tile course) is a two-trade interface that reliably stalls: with separate subs the tiler either waits on the EPDM or leaves the top courses and returns (second-visit charge GBP 150-250 plus 3-5 lost days). One sub carrying both tickets prices the package ~5-7% under the sum of trades and, more importantly, saves 1-2 scaffold weeks - scaffold is 'in the bill' but hire extensions run GBP 100-150/week, and every roof week also blocks the follow-on internal trades. Realistic compression: a coordinated single-sub roof package closes the roof in 2.5-3 weeks vs 4-5 with split trades. NET POSITION: the roof bill lands ~GBP 17,000-17,500 after these moves (seconds PIR, free-issued sundries, written price-work rates, Ubiflex, single sub) with zero spec or kerb-appeal loss - the remaining big number is the GBP 7,500 truss supply, which is a design/procurement question, not a details one.

killed: KILLED - Cold-deck EPDM over the habitable loft: a crown roof's hidden flat centre cannot achieve the 50mm cross-ventilated void a cold deck needs (no through-flow past four hips into a concealed centre); condensation over a fully-finished storey = Building Control refusal under BS 5250 and an automatic warranty-surveyor bounce (NHBC-type standards effectively prohibit cold decks over habitable rooms). Must be a warm deck: ~140-150mm PIR above deck + AVCL to hit U 0.15. Adds ~GBP 750, saves nothing.

KILLED - Mortar-only ridges/hips: BS 5534:2014+A2 requires mechanical fixing of all ridge and hip units; BS 8612 governs the dry-fix systems. Mortar-bedded-only is non-compliant, uninsurable, and a mortgage-survey snag. The four hips (~20-22m) must be dry-fixed; this money must appear as an explicit line, not be 'saved'.

KILLED - Under-fixing tiles at 41 degrees: BS 5534 fixing calculation for Birmingham wind exposure at 41-degree pitch on interlocking concrete requires at least the manufacturer's calculated fix (typically every tile nailed and/or clipped) plus twice-fixed perimeter courses (eaves, top course at the flat junction, hips). There is no lawful saving in fixings.

KILLED - Non-breathable (Type 1F felt) underlay swap: the pitched skirt discharges into a concealed pitch-to-flat junction that ventilates poorly; a vapour-permeable underlay plus high-level ventilation at the junction is the only defensible spec for a finished loft. Total saving from felt would be ~GBP 75-100 on 75m2 - trivial against condensation risk. Dead.

KILLED - Any insulation build-up missing U 0.15: 100mm PIR between rafters gives ~U 0.21 and fails the stated Part L target; BC/SAP bounce. Compliant slope build-up is ~120mm PIR between rafters + 25-37.5mm insulated lining under. Also note: the GBP 18,500 bill contains NO roof insulation line at all - that is a scope hole, not a saving.

KILLED as DOUBLE-COUNTS - (a) 'switch tiling to price-work': the GBP 4,150 line already is price-work (~GBP 1,100 tile supply + ~GBP 40/m2 fixing, matching 2026 market GBP 40-60/m2); (b) 'buy EPDM supply-only online': already assumed in the GBP 1,500 line; (c) 'swap lead for Ubiflex': already the GBP 1,800 line, and 2026 data shows Ubiflex saves labour not material vs Code 4 at flashing widths - no second bite; (d) 'seconds/discount tile channel': GBP 14-15/m2 Edgemere-class IS the discount-channel price - cannot be claimed again.

KILLED - Cut roof instead of trusses, or shell/unfinished loft phasing: a site-cut crown roof carrying a habitable storey needs SE redesign, steels and far more carpentry labour than the truss saving; phasing is excluded by the brief (fully finished, no phasing). Also kills any 'loose joist attic floor' idea - the SE will not sign it.
revised_bill: STRUCTURE - Truncated (crown) attic truss package, 8.6m span x ~11 no. at 600cc + 2 hip-end sets, girders, bracing, metalwork, delivered with hiab off-load, RE-TENDERED to 3 fabricators off the SE's loading spec: GBP 5,200 (was GBP 7,500)

LABOUR (structure) - Carpentry erection on price-work: set out, hand-set trusses, bracing to fabricator layout, hip framing, 18mm OSB3 firrings/deck to flat centre: GBP 3,750 (was GBP 3,500-4,500, fixed at measured rate)

COVERINGS - ~75m2 Edgemere-class interlocking concrete slate supplied ~GBP 14.50/m2, vapour-permeable underlay, treated battens, BS 5534 calculated fixings (every-tile fix, twice-fixed perimeters), price-work fixing: GBP 4,150 (unchanged - already at market floor)
DETAILS (ridge/hip) - Dry-fix hip and ridge system to BS 8612, ~20-22m across four hips, kit + fixing on price-work with scaffold standing: GBP 850 (NEW explicit line - was hidden/absent)

FLAT CENTRE - ~28m2 WARM deck: AVCL on deck, 140-150mm flat-roof PIR, ClassicBond-class 1.2mm EPDM supply kit incl. upstands and edge trims to the pitch-to-flat junction, labour: GBP 2,250 (was GBP 1,500 cold deck - killed)

INSULATION (pitched skirt/room-in-roof envelope to U 0.15) - 120mm PIR between rafters (~20 sheets at ~GBP 45 ex VAT) + 25-37.5mm PIR-backed lining extra-over, collars/ashlar walls, fitted: GBP 1,650 (NEW line - missing entirely from the GBP 18,500 bill; buy early, 2026 PIR shortage reported)

RAINWATER / FASCIA / FLASHINGS - Ubiflex B3 abutment flashings and soakers, fascia/soffit with over-fascia ventilation plus high-level vents at the flat junction, uPVC gutters and downpipes: GBP 1,800 (unchanged - already VE'd, market-verified fair)
verdict.total_and_saving: Honest compliant total: GBP 19,650. Versus the GBP 18,500 headline that is +GBP 1,150, and that is the truthful answer: the old bill was ~GBP 3,450 under-scoped (no insulation line, cold deck, no dry-fix money). The truss re-tender claws back ~GBP 2,300 of that. Any figure below ~GBP 19.5k for this roof is a bill that Building Control, the warranty surveyor or the SE will re-inflate on site.
verdict.best_lever: Re-tender the attic-truss package: send the SE's loading spec and the planning roof geometry to three truss fabricators (not via the builder) and buy direct, delivered hiab. Market data puts 8-8.6m attic trusses at ~GBP 163-400 each, so an 11-truss crown package with hip sets should land GBP 4,800-5,500 delivered against the GBP 7,500 quoted - a GBP 2,000-2,500 saving on one purchase order, with zero compliance or kerb-appeal risk.
verdict.do_not_touch: Do not touch the tiling line (GBP 4,150) or the tile/fixing spec: supply is already at discount-channel money (~GBP 14-15/m2) and fixing is already price-work at the bottom of the 2026 GBP 40-60/m2 band - any further cut can only come out of BS 5534 fixings or the 41-degree kerb-appeal skirt the planners approved, and both are non-negotiable.
verified_facts: Attic trusses ~8m span average ~GBP 163/truss supply (range roughly GBP 80-400 by span/complexity); full-house attic packages GBP 7,000-12,000 - confirming GBP 7,500 supply-only for an 11-truss extension package is top-of-market and the re-tender target of GBP 4,800-5,500 is realistic. Sources: myjobquote.co.uk/costs/roof-truss, checkatrade.com/blog/cost-guides/truss-roof-cost, mybuilder.com/roofing/price-guides/roof-trusses-cost

Roof tiling labour 2026: GBP 40-60/m2 for straightforward interlocking price-work (full supply-and-fix GBP 85-130/m2) - the existing GBP 4,150 line already embeds bottom-of-band labour, so 'go price-work' is a double-count with no headroom. Sources: quote-guru.co.uk/blog/en/roofing-job-pricing-guide, costestimator.co.uk, homebuilding.co.uk/advice/cost-of-tiling-a-roof

Dry ridge/hip 2026: GBP 35-65/m installed, dry hip ~GBP 300-400/hip, and BS 5534/BS 8612 make mechanical ridge/hip fixing mandatory - mortar-only is dead on arrival at Building Control; ~GBP 850 for ~20-22m on price-work with scaffold up is the honest number. Sources: mybuilder.com dry-ridge cost guide, checkatrade.com dry-ridge cost guide, ajrroofing.uk

120mm PIR (2400x1200, 2.88m2) ~GBP 40-50/sheet ex VAT (~GBP 14-17/m2) with bulk breaks to ~GBP 35; a 2026 PIR supply shortage is reported - order insulation with the truss package, not later. Sources: insulationpoint.co.uk, insulationwholesale.co.uk

Ubiflex B3 vs Code 4 lead 2026: material prices near-parity at flashing widths; the saving is in labour already captured by the GBP 1,800 line - keep it, no second saving exists. Sources: buildwiz.uk lead-free flashing guide, roofinglines.co.uk
